---
title: Mastermind ship collector
description: The Cron Control job that records what is live per app and environment for the Mastermind Ship screen, with its credentials, request budget, stop fence and operation envelope.
updatedAt: "2026-11-22"
---

The Ship screen ([web and mobile](/platform/features/mobile-mastermind#ship))
reads one snapshot that the `mastermind-ship` job in
[Cron Control](/build/devops/cloudflare-cron-control) writes to the
[Mastermind store](/build/devops/mastermind-store) every two minutes. Owners
can also run it with **Check now**. Web serves the snapshot owner-only at
`GET /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/ship` from a five-second per-colo cache;
`?fresh=1`, the read after Check now, skips it and replaces the cached
copy.

## What each run reads

| Source | Requests | Facts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub, per repository | One conditional probe of the newest Actions run per repository (`If-None-Match`; a 304 costs no rate limit), then one batched GraphQL query, plus at most two deployment follow-up queries | The newest successful deployment per tracked environment, the CI rollup of its commit, and the commits on the branch newer than the production commit for the app's paths |
| Cloudflare | One deployments read per Worker script, plus one version read the first time a version id is seen. A script the account does not have (404) reads as no Worker for that environment, not a source failure; every script answering 404 fails the source, since that means a wrong account or token | The active version, its traffic share, its deploy time and the SHA from its message or tag |

The probe is skipped on **Check now** and when the last full read is four
minutes old, so a read is reused for at most four minutes, inside the
clients' six-minute stale window. A 304 leaves `okAt` at the last full read.
A GraphQL answer with `errors` or a missing repository fails the source
instead of replacing its facts. When an environment's first page of
deployments holds no success and more pages exist, the run reads up to two
more pages (100 deployments each, one query for every such environment).
Past those it keeps the previous live release, marked with the newest
attempt's state, rather than recording none. Only a newest successful
deployment reads as Deployed; a newer failed, inactive or unfinished one
reads as Deploy failed or Deploying. The
catalog of apps, environments, paths and Worker scripts is
`apps/cron-control/src/processors/mastermind-ship/catalog.ts`. Apps outside this repository default to their known repositories; one
without a known repository stays "not configured" until
`MASTERMIND_SHIP_REPOS` names it. Each repository is its own source, so an
unreadable repository marks only its own rows.

Each source records `checkedAt`, `okAt` (data last confirmed current),
`retryAt` and a closed-set `problem`. A failed source keeps its last-known
facts with the old `okAt`, so a client always shows how old a row is.
The snapshot holds SHAs, times, environment and script names, CI states and
counts only. ETags, installation ids and cached version facts live under a
separate store key that Web never serves.

## Configuration

| Name | Where | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` | Cron Control text | Add `mastermind-ship` to enable the schedule and Check now. |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_URL` | Cron Control secret | HTTPS origin of the Mastermind store. |
| `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKEN` | Cron Control secret | A store service token; add it to the store's `MASTERMIND_STORE_TOKENS` rotation list. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_GITHUB_APP_ID`, `MASTERMIND_SHIP_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | Cron Control secrets | Preferred: a GitHub App installed on each tracked owner with read-only Actions, Checks, Commit statuses, Contents, Deployments and Metadata. The key is PKCS#8 PEM (`openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in app.pem`). Each run mints a one-hour installation token. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_GITHUB_TOKEN` | Cron Control secret | Fallback when no App is set: one read-only token for every tracked owner. Never the shared fleet token. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN` | Cron Control secret | Account token with Workers Scripts Read. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_REPOS` | Cron Control text | `app=owner/name[@branch]`, comma-separated, for the apps tracked outside this repository (catalog ids). Other app ids and malformed entries are ignored. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_CHECK_TOKEN` | Cron Control and Web secret | At least 32 characters; authorizes `POST /mastermind-ship/check`. Mint it with [shared-secret-write](/build/devops/shared-secret-write), which writes Cron Control and the web Workers in one run; the store token's mint also writes Cron Control. |
| `CRON_CONTROL` | Web service binding (api-core family only) | Reaches `tuturuuu-cron-control`, which has no public ingress (no workers.dev, no routes). Declared in `apps/web/cloudflare.config.ts`; Cron Control's own config needs no binding to receive it. |
| `MASTERMIND_SHIP_CHECK_ORIGIN` | Web | Only without the binding (local runs): an HTTPS origin for Cron Control; defaults to `WEB_CRON_GATE_ORIGIN`. |

Without GitHub or Cloudflare credentials the job still writes a snapshot in
which those sources read `unconfigured`, and makes no provider request.

## Bounds and stop fence

- The job adds no Worker trigger: it is admitted every second minute of the
  existing one-minute trigger (`everyMinutes` in `jobs.ts`), so the reviewed
  trigger set and its parity baseline are unchanged. Odd minutes cost no
  ledger or network call.

- One attempt per slot; the next slot is the retry. A run has a 40-second
  deadline, 32 provider requests at most and two store requests (one read,
  one write of two rows).
- A 403 or 429 backs the source off until `Retry-After` or the rate-limit
  reset, clamped to one minute to one hour; a GraphQL budget below 200 points
  backs off until its reset. Backed-off sources make no request.
- Check now goes through the same ledger claim as the schedule. The last
  claimed slot rate-limits checks to one per 30 seconds across both paths,
  the lease refuses overlapping runs, and Web adds six requests a minute per
  owner.
- A slot in which a provider call failed and no configured source is `ok`
  is `failed` and counts against the failure budget, so a revoked
  credential stops the job after five slots. One failing source beside a
  working one is `degraded`.
- **Check now resumes a failure-budget stop.** Cron Control's operator
  routes have no public ingress, so the owner's Check now (admitted by the
  30-second limit) resumes a job its five-slot failure budget stopped, then
  runs it. An operator stop is never lifted this way; Check now answers
  `stopped`. A resumed job that keeps failing stops again after five slots.
- Durable stops: `POST /control/jobs/mastermind-ship/stop` with the operator
  token (Cron Control has no public ingress, so this runs only from an
  operator session with access to the Worker, never from Web; Web holds only
  the check token) (survives restarts; resume opens a new generation), five consecutive
  failed or unknown slots, or the store's own fence (`stopped` ends the run
  without charging the failure budget). The fence is checked before each
  owner, each Worker read and the write.

Regressions: `apps/cron-control/src/mastermind-ship.test.ts` (default-off,
the snapshot and its sanitization, unconfigured sources, the 304 reuse
window, backoff with carried facts, stop across a restart, the store fence,
the failure budget, Check now auth, rate limit and stop) and
`src/processors/mastermind-ship/units.test.ts` (repository config, the
query, capped pending counts, GraphQL budget backoff, App tokens, version
caching and the request budget).
`apps/web/src/app/api/v1/mastermind/fleet/ship/ship-route.test.ts` runs the
collector's output through Web's schema and covers owner-only reads,
tampered values and the Check now relay.

## Operation envelope

At 720 slots a day a normal run makes one or two GitHub requests per
repository (one more with App tokens), nine Cloudflare deployment reads, two
store requests and about fourteen ledger calls. For three repositories that
is about 2,200 to 6,500 GitHub requests, 6,500
Cloudflare API reads and 1,440 store row writes a day (of the store's 50,000
daily write budget). Check now adds at most one run per 30 seconds. The
failure case is capped by the request budget per run and the five-slot
failure stop.

## Enable

1. Create the GitHub App (or token) and the Cloudflare token; set the Cron
   Control secrets above and add the store token to the store's rotation list.
2. Set `MASTERMIND_SHIP_CHECK_TOKEN` on Cron Control and on Web's
   `tuturuuu-web-vinext-api-core` Worker, and deploy api-core with its
   `CRON_CONTROL` binding.
3. Add `mastermind-ship` to `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` and deploy Cron
   Control. Press **Check now**; it answers `checked` and the Ship screen
   shows fresh `okAt` stamps.

To stop the job without operator access, remove it from
`CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` and deploy Cron Control: disabled jobs make no
ledger or network call, and Check now answers `disabled`.
